scheme_name: Registered BOC Workers in case of an Accidental Death (JKBOCWWB)
description:
The Jammu and Kashmir Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board scheme is designed to provide financial assistance to registered construction workers in the event of accidental death. 

This scheme was launched as part of the broader initiative to support the welfare of construction workers in the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir. 

The scheme aims to provide immediate financial relief to the families of registered workers who meet with accidental deaths while engaged in construction work. 

The scheme was officially implemented in the year 2020. 

The primary objective of this welfare scheme is to ensure that the families of deceased workers receive a financial benefit that can aid them in coping with the loss of their primary breadwinner. 

The scheme targets the families of registered construction workers who have been contributing to the building and construction sector. 

The specific goal is to provide a monetary benefit of INR 2 lakh to the family of the deceased worker. 

This amount is intended to assist with immediate financial needs such as funeral expenses and other urgent requirements following the death of the worker. 

To be eligible for the benefits under this scheme, the applicant must be a registered construction worker under the Jammu and Kashmir Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

The worker must have been actively engaged in construction work at the time of the accident leading to death. 

There are no specific age limits for eligibility under this scheme. 

However, the worker must have completed the registration process with the Board and must have been in good standing at the time of the incident. 

The income criteria for eligibility are not strictly defined in terms of upper limits. 

However, it is generally expected that the worker is engaged in construction work as their primary source of income. 

To apply for the benefits under this scheme, the family of the deceased worker must follow a specific application process. 

The first step is to obtain a death certificate from the relevant local authorities. 

This document serves as proof of the worker's death due to an accident. 

Next, the family must gather the worker's registration details from the Jammu and Kashmir Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

This includes the registration number and any other relevant identification details. 

The family must also provide proof of the relationship to the deceased worker. 

Documents such as an Aadhaar card or other government-issued identification can serve this purpose. 

The application form for the scheme can be obtained from the official website of the Jammu and Kashmir Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

Once the application form is filled out, it must be submitted along with the required documents to the nearest office of the Board. 

The application must be submitted within a specific timeframe following the death of the worker to ensure timely processing. 

The processing of applications typically takes around 30 days from the date of submission. 

Once approved, the financial assistance of INR 2 lakh is disbursed directly to the bank account of the beneficiary. 

The scheme is implemented by the Jammu and Kashmir Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

This Board operates under the Department of Labour and Employment of the Government of Jammu and Kashmir. 

For any queries or assistance, individuals can contact the Board through their official helpline or visit their local office. 

The contact details for the Jammu and Kashmir Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board can be found on their official website. 

The scheme is part of a larger framework of welfare initiatives aimed at improving the living conditions of construction workers in the region. 

The Board also provides various other benefits such as health insurance, maternity benefits, and educational assistance for the children of registered workers. 

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is critical in ensuring that families do not face financial hardships in the wake of an unexpected tragedy. 

The scheme reflects the commitment of the Jammu and Kashmir government to support its workforce, particularly those engaged in hazardous occupations like construction. 

In terms of statistics, the Jammu and Kashmir Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board has registered over 1.5 lakh workers since its inception. 

The Board has also disbursed significant amounts in various welfare schemes to support the construction workforce in the region. 

The accidental death benefit scheme is one of the most crucial components of the welfare measures provided to these workers. 

The government continues to promote awareness about this scheme to ensure that eligible families are informed and can access the benefits. 

Regular workshops and outreach programs are conducted to educate workers about their rights and the benefits available to them. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's efforts to create a safety net for workers in the construction sector. 

The construction industry in Jammu and Kashmir has been a significant contributor to the local economy. 

However, it is also known for its risks and hazards, making such welfare schemes essential for worker protection. 

The Board regularly reviews and updates its welfare schemes to meet the evolving needs of the workforce. 

In conclusion, the Registered BOC Workers in case of an Accidental Death scheme is a vital initiative that provides essential financial support to the families of construction workers in Jammu and Kashmir. 

The scheme not only alleviates immediate financial burdens but also serves as a recognition of the contributions made by these workers to the region's development. 

By ensuring that families receive timely assistance, the scheme plays a crucial role in enhancing the overall welfare of construction workers in Jammu and Kashmir. 

The commitment of the Jammu and Kashmir government to the welfare of its workers is evident in the establishment and implementation of this scheme. 

Families of registered workers are encouraged to familiarize themselves with the application process and ensure they have all necessary documentation ready in case of an unfortunate event. 

This proactive approach can help ensure that they receive the financial assistance they are entitled to without unnecessary delays. 

The scheme stands as a model for similar initiatives across other states in India, aiming to protect the rights and welfare of construction workers nationwide.
